title: SG2 (CX-123 rule 24): card update, group places and free copies read their counters only in their exact shape
body:
## What changes

These gates read a Redis counter with `Number(...)` and no shape check. On an unknown reply they let the work through: `NaN > n` is false, and `null`, `true` and `""` read as within the cap. Each now refuses **before** the Stripe call, the email, any write or the delivery. Group places are also reworked so that a lost reply never loses a place and never gives one too many.

**`lib/card-update.ts` `openCardUpdate`:** an unknown count gives `error`, with no Stripe call.

**`lib/free.ts`:**
- `requestCopy` (`within`, per connection and per address): an unknown count gives `error`, with no email and no link kept.
- `spendClaim`: an unknown count throws `UnknownReplyError`, and no file is released.

**`lib/group-buy.ts`:**
- **Places are counted by marks.** A place is the address's own mark (`HSETNX`), and the places taken are the number of marks (`HLEN`), in one pipeline. There is no separate counter that could be left holding a paid place for no one. The address works as the operation's token: a retry by the same address reuses its mark and never counts twice. After a lost reply, the next open finds out from its own mark whether the place is its own, and resumes the delivery if it is.
- **"already" requires a confirmed delivery:** a valid grant record whose `job` is this purchase. A delivery without a mark gets its mark written back.
- **Exact shapes:**
  - The mark is valid only as a JSON object with `e` (a non-empty string), `at` (an integer of at least 1), and optional `h` and `d`; nothing else.
  - The grant record is valid only as an object with a non-empty `job` and a numeric `at`.
  - `HGET null` means absent. Anything else is unknown and throws before any completed or already answer, with the mark kept.
  - After a refused grant, an `HGET` of `null` is inconsistent: it throws and the pending mark is kept.
- **One open per address at a time:** a 30-second hold with a random token. It is released by one compare-and-delete script (`marktmorgen:group-place-release:v1`), so an open that outlives its 30 seconds never deletes the next open's hold. The in-memory Redis gets that one script's branch, with Codex V's leave.
- **The group's email counter:** `SET … EX 86400 NX` and `INCR` in one pipeline, so a lost reply never leaves the counter without its 24 h expiry.
- **Order admission:** the reservation of a refused open is given back. A completed open is settled once, after its "done" mark.
- **Cost of a later open that finds the place already done:** a cheap read first (4 commands, down from 12). An open that delivers costs 26 commands, up from 21.

**`app/[handle]/group/[group]/page.tsx` and `lib/buyer-words/giving.ts`:** a new `opening` notice, used when taking a place throws: "We could not finish opening your place. Open the link again in a moment. If it was already yours, nothing changes." It is in the 7 languages, chosen by `placeNotice()`, and never accepted from `?status=`.

body:
## Summary
Finding E-2 of the SG1 security audit (LIGHT). The Stripe checkout session id (`cs_…`) and the PayPal order id are capabilities. Holding one opens:
- the download and the buyer's email;
- the verified review and Discord;
- the call room or rescheduling, and the `?pkg=` token;
- on PayPal, every purchase of that email.

Until now they were sent as `eventID` / `event_id` / `order_id` / `transaction_id` to Meta, TikTok, Pinterest, Google, X and Reddit. They went from the buyer's browser (pixels on the thanks page) and from our server (conversions in `lib/ad-events.ts`, including renewal invoices `in_…`, which `lib/review-proof.ts` accepts as proof of purchase). The reservation was posted in the channel ("RESERVA:" line); `docs/reservations/claude4.md` is not touched.

## What changed
- **`lib/ad-events.ts`:** new `adEventId(id)`. It is `ev_` followed by 32 hex characters: an HMAC-SHA256 of the id under a key used only for this, derived from the root secret (`deriveKey("marktmorgen/ad-event-id/v1")`, the same mechanism as `lib/secret-box.ts`).
  - It is stable, so the browser pixel and the server conversion still deduplicate.
  - It cannot be reversed. It is keyed, not a plain hash, because a PayPal order id is short and partly guessable.
  - When the root secret is missing, it returns `""`: nothing is sent with an id and the purchase pixel does not fire. The raw id is never sent instead.
  - `conversionOf` (`cs_`) and `sendRenewals` (`in_`) use it. So `event_id`, Pinterest `order_id` and GA4 `transaction_id` carry the derived id.
- **`app/[handle]/thanks/page.tsx`:** the six purchase events pass `id: adEventId(…)`, computed on the server. The raw session id goes only to our own `/api/store/ads-event`, as `order`; the PayPal event sends no `order`.
- **`components/store-pixels.tsx`:** `PixelEvent` gets an optional `order` field. X `conversion_id` and Reddit `conversionId` now get the derived id without any change to their modules.
- **`tests/server-conversions.test.ts` and `tests/numbers-five.test.ts`:** they now expect the derived id.

Rule 30 (same pattern elsewhere):
- GA4 `transaction_id` (browser and server), Pinterest, X and Reddit are covered by this change.
- The lead id (`ld_`, random) is not a key to anything and is left as it is.
- The server's `event_source_url` already drops the query (`pageOf`).

**Not fixed here (follow-up unit, proposal):** the third-party scripts themselves read `location.href`, which still holds `?session_id=cs_…` (or `?order=` on PayPal). Meta's `dl`, TikTok, Pinterest, GA `page_location`, X and Reddit all send it. The Referer does not leak (`strict-origin-when-cross-origin`).
- Proposed fix: `success_url` goes through our own route, which keeps the id in a short-lived HttpOnly cookie (or an opaque server token) and redirects with a 303 to `/@handle/thanks` without the id.

title: CRM: a person's field value written atomically under the people lock
body:
## What changes (review of 1d585ef4; owner orders C3-119, C3-123 and C3-125; Codex G and G2)

**The race.** `setValue` raced `forgetCrmPerson`. In one ordering the value came back after the person was erased, and part of its space was never paid for (counted 768 against 592 stored, and 352 against 592).

**The final design:**
- **Deletion mark and generation.** `forgetCrmPerson` writes a mark, `nl:crm:erased:<statsId>:<personKey>`, before deleting anything. It also adds one to the person's generation, `nl:crm:gen:`. Both keys are hashed and hold only a time or a number. They last at most 31 days (`ERASED_MARK_SECONDS`).
- **Writing a value.** `setValue` writes through `SET_CRM_VALUE` v6. In the same atomic step as the write it refuses when:
  - the mark is there;
  - the save carries another generation than the person's;
  - a workflow step's own take of the lease is gone.
  A value is either refused or deleted with the rest. Space is reserved first and given back from what the write replaced, so what is counted is what is kept.
- **Only the server takes the mark away** (`personReturned`), when the person really comes back: a paid order, a confirmed sign-up or place, or a free product claimed through the emailed link. A form never does.
- **A page's signed mark.** Each page carries a mark signed by the server (`pageMark`: the generation it read and when). It is valid for `PAGE_MARK_SECONDS`, one hour less than the mark and the generation are kept. A save without a valid mark is refused as `"stale"` (409). The entry stays on the screen, to save again after a reload.
- **A workflow run's own take** (`leaseScore`: a score drawn for each take of the queue). Each of these checks that exact score:
  - the field write;
  - queuing the next step (`QUEUE_IF_LEASED` v2);
  - putting back and finishing (`DROP_OWN_LEASES`);
  - the batch's held check.
  So an old run under way when the person was deleted neither writes, nor goes on with the steps, nor takes away the lease of a later run that took the same entry.
- **Cost (C3-125).** A field saved from the studio is counted as `CRM_VALUE_SAVE_UNITS` = 2 studio requests, taken before anything is read. It runs within 9 trips for the owner and 12 for a teammate (`CRM_VALUE_SAVE_TRIPS`), with `CRM_VALUE_SAVE_COMMANDS` = 30 commands and `CRM_VALUE_SAVE_BYTES`. Workflows take no extra request.
- **LEVE 3.** An edit of a deal that is already deleted answers `"gone"` in the preflight, without touching space.
- **LEVE 4.** Already covered on main: `tests/crm-deal-conflict.test.ts`.

No price, limit, commission, flag, tax gate or review changes.

## Codex G2's rounds

- **485023fe.**
  - **A page read before a deletion could save once the generation lapsed and the session was renewed.** Fixed by the signed page mark.
  - **An old run wrote a field under a later run's take.** Fixed by `SET_CRM_VALUE` v6 checking the take's score.
  - **LEVE:** the privacy text no longer says a form takes the mark away.
- **3cb72e67.**
  - **The old run still queued its next steps and took the later run's lease away.** Fixed: queuing, putting back and finishing all check the take's own score.
  - **LEVE:** this description now states the final cost (2 requests; 9 or 12 trips).

## Tests

- **`crm-person-room`**: the interleaving, with space counted against space stored, an erasure between the reservation and the write, and the mark's value and TTL. The race cases fail on main.
- **`crm-contact-writes`**, through the real route:
  - the whole save at the largest value, within the figures above;
  - someone who came back is saved;

title: Broken move repair: delete the untouched copy however the store changed since
body:
## What changes (light findings of the #2140 review)

**The problem.** `settleDoubledStore` deleted the copy a broken move left behind only when the two records were equal apart from the address. But the store's own record keeps getting written by its id: daily plan jobs, Stripe's answers, imports. Hours after the failure the two records almost always differed, so the repair left the case for a person, and a login by the emailed link waited ("move-busy").

**The fix:**
- `moveAccount` takes an optional `onCopy`. Just before the old record is taken away, it reports the fingerprint of what it wrote at the new address (`copyPrint`: the record without its address).
- The move route saves that fingerprint with the move's record (`noteMoveCopy`). Each move gets its own token of 64 hex from the server when its record is written (`markBrokenMove`), and the fingerprint is written by one script (`NOTE_MOVE_COPY`) only where the record still carries that same token: a move already cleared, or replaced by another (of other addresses, or of the same two again), is never written over (Codex H, C3-133). This is best effort: without the fingerprint, the old comparison of the whole records stays.
- The repair deletes the copy (the record the handle does not point to) while it still has that fingerprint, whatever the store did since. A copy somebody edited is still never deleted.
- `tests/move-repair-script.test.ts` builds the support script the same way it is built, with `lib/move-repair.ts` swapped for a stand-in. It checks two things:
  - `--repair` and `--clear` change nothing without `--yes-production`, including with look-alike flags;

title: Studio people page: the 50 KB its request includes are spent once
body:
## What changes (C3-112 (2), Revisor 3 cycle 71 on #1960)

**The bug.** Three helpers each counted 0 units up to `PAGE_INCLUDED_BYTES`: `agendaReadUnits` (lib/person-agenda.ts), `ledgerUnits` (lib/segments.ts) and `sentUnits` (lib/sent-bytes.ts). But `UNIT_COST.studio` covers 50 KB for the whole page. So a visit to /studio/people could read and send several parts of up to 50 KB each, all paid by one request.

**The fix (option (a)):**
- `IncludedBytes` in `lib/sent-bytes.ts` is one budget per request. `take(bytes, perUnit)` works like this:
  - a part that fits in what is left counts 0 and spends that much of the budget;
  - a part that does not fit counts on its own `ceil(bytes / MB)`, exactly what it counted before.
  - So no part counts less than before, and the page never gets more than 50 KB free in total.
- An invalid size throws; it never counts as zero.
- `app/studio/people/page.tsx` makes one budget. It passes it to `addressForPerson` and to `agendaData`, which passes it on to `agendaReadUnits`, `buyerLedger` and `sentUnits`. Inside `buyerLedger`, the copy and the rest of the reading share that same budget.
- `buyerLedger` changes in two ways:
  - its `GETRANGE` reads only up to what was covered;
  - a copy whose size is unknown throws `LedgerNotCounted` and nothing is read.
- Callers that read one part alone keep their own fresh budget.
- Text fix: "N open tasks across your buyers" becomes "N open tasks across the people in your store".

**Worst case of /studio/people** (each part 50,000 bytes; tasks of 2 people, 40,560 bytes):

| Case | Bytes | Before | Now |

| with `?who=` | 290,560 | 1 request | 6 requests (parts `[0,1,1,1,1,1]`) |

639 [GL7](19): a workflow's earlier versions, and putting one back, as sales pages already have.

- **Unit 1** (`lib/flow-versions.ts`):
  - Each save that changes what a workflow does keeps the version before it: the newest ten, newest first, under `nl:wf:ver:<listId>:<flowId>`. They are counted in the store's data room in slot `wv:<flowId>`. A full room keeps none and never stops an ordinary save. Switching on or off keeps none.
  - The mail route lists them (`flow-versions`) and puts one back (`flow-restore`). Putting one back is a `saveFlow` of that content, checked whole against the store as it is now.
  - A removed workflow's versions go with it, and so do every workflow's versions when the store is deleted.
  - Registered in `lib/data-families.ts` (counted, erased on closing) and `tests/store-data-registry.ts`.
- **Unit 2** (`components/workflow-versions.tsx`):
  - "Earlier versions" sits beside "Runs" in the email studio, with "Put this version back" on each version.
  - It says what is kept, that on/off stays, and what happens to people already in the workflow: same step number, and a run past the last step ends, as when a step is removed.
- **Codex G2's four MEDIUMs on 243c0e053** (1743533e1):
  1. **A pause is never undone.** The workflows are written only over the text they were read from (`WRITE_FLOWS_IF`, in `saveFlow`, `setFlowActive` and `removeFlow`). Each change is read afresh and tried again up to three times, then it is unconfirmed. Putting a version back takes on/off from that same read, so a pause made meanwhile stays paused.
  2. **The room is never below what is held.** A version is pushed only onto the list its room was counted from (`KEEP_FLOW_VERSION`). A list that cannot be read whole keeps none. A retried save does not keep the same version twice. Room is given back only once Redis confirms the list deleted.
  3. **Unknown is never "none".** A history that cannot be read whole, or that holds an entry that is not a version of this workflow, answers 503 `flow_versions_unavailable`. The studio says it could not be read and that this does not mean there are none; never "No earlier version yet".
  4. **The undo is always there.** Putting a version back keeps the one in use first. Without room for it, nothing is put back and nothing changes (409 `history_room`, with its own sentence in the studio).
- **Codex G2's residual MEDIUM and Codex Reviewer 2's MEDIUM on 1743533e1** (dd5bd4f9a, main merged in):
  1. **The room moves by what each push or deletion changes, never set to a total.**
     - A push refused because the list changed used to read the list again and set the room to that total. A newer push landing in between was cut (2240 needed, 1104 counted).
     - A push now lands only on the list it was counted from, so the room moves by what it changes: taken first when it grows, and given back when written and smaller. When refused, only its own taking goes back, with no second read.
     - Deleting a workflow's versions is one script (`DROP_FLOW_VERSIONS`). It answers, from the same step, how many versions it removed and how long they were, and only that is given back.
  2. **A store deleted takes every workflow's versions with it.** `forgetStoreWorkflows` left `nl:wf:ver` behind. A deletion that is not confirmed throws and is never reported done.
- **Codex G's retention findings on e4f446e6 and fbf2a215, and Codex Reviewer 2's cycles 75, 77 and 84** (fbf2a2151, 436472341):
  1. **Every list keeps an index of its workflows with versions** (`nl:wf:ver:idx:<list>`). A push adds to it in the same step, and a deletion removes from it in the same step. The store's deletion uses it, so it also finds the versions of a workflow removed earlier whose deletion was not confirmed.
  2. **A version is pushed only while its own workflow is still saved.** `KEEP_FLOW_VERSION` v3 compares each saved workflow's top-level id, never a step's id. A save that finishes after its workflow was removed pushes nothing.
  3. **The store's deletion goes in this order:** runs first (while the workflows are still listed), then the workflows, then every version found through the index. If a try fails, another try can still finish it.
  4. **A removal whose versions are not confirmed deleted is never reported as done.** It answers `history_unconfirmed` (503).
- **Known limit (accepted by Claude 4, C4-20261106-1805-C3-106):** when a removal answers `history_unconfirmed`, the creator cannot try the removal again from the studio. The versions and their room stay until the store is deleted, which finds them through the index. No data is at risk, and the cost is the room already counted. A later, low-priority unit may let the creator repeat the removal. The studio says: "Removal of “<name>” could not be confirmed. Reload to check its current status. The sequence was removed, but its earlier versions could not be confirmed deleted just now. They are kept listed and are deleted with your store's data."

title: 513 [PF1] unit 3b: one product's stock hold, no lock held while Stripe opens the checkout
body:
## 513 [PF1] unit 3b: one product's stock hold, no lock held while Stripe opens the checkout

Queue item 513 [PF1], unit 3b. Stacked on #1730 (`claude2/pf1-cart-stock`).

**The defect, found by the review of unit 3.** A limited product bought on its own holds a unit with `withStockHold` (`lib/stock.ts`). Its lock had two problems:
- it was a plain value (`SET NX EX 15`), deleted in `finally` without checking whose it was;
- it was held while Stripe opened the checkout. That opening can retry, with a 20-second timeout each time, so it can take longer than the lock's 15 seconds.

If the lock ran out mid-way, a second checkout could take it, count the same last unit as free, and open too. Its `DEL` then deleted the second checkout's lock.

**The fix.** `withStockHold` is now a cart of one: `withCartStockHolds(store, [product], open)`, from unit 3.
- Its lock is a token (`lib/redis-lock.ts`), let go only by its holder.
- The lock is renewed before anything is written; a lock lost while Stripe was asked about older holds writes nothing.
- A provisional hold is written before the lock is let go, so no lock is held while Stripe opens the checkout.
- The checkout's own hold replaces the provisional one. If its write is not acknowledged, the checkout is closed at Stripe and never returned.
- The return shape, `held`, and unlimited products (no Redis at all) are unchanged for every caller: the product checkout, moving members, welcome and win-back offers.
- An unreadable count still throws, as before.
- Each count's question to Stripe about a hold that ran out now waits at most 2 seconds (`CHECK_MS`). An answer that does not come in time counts the unit as used, the safe way to be wrong. The lock lasts long enough for every count to ask its most times.

**Tests that pinned the old commands.** Two tests listed the exact Redis commands of the old path (`SET, HGETALL, HSET, DEL`). They now list the new ones, and they assert what they always meant, now more strictly:
- **no checkout returned without a confirmed hold write.** The provisional hold's write must now be acknowledged *before* anything is opened, so an unknown acknowledgment opens nothing at all, where before it opened a checkout and then threw it away. The checkout's own hold's write is checked separately, with sixteen malformed replies, sparse arrays included.
- **unreadable inventory never opens a checkout,** and the lock is let go by compare-and-delete (`EVAL`), not a bare `DEL`.

While doing this, a sparse reply (`Array(2)`) was found to pass as two acknowledgments in unit 3's code. It is fixed in #1730 with its own test.

**State:** tested in this PR. Not merged, not published. Nothing is on sale (`PLANS_ON_SALE` false).

## Tests

All 26 test files that read `lib/stock.ts`, the product or cart checkout or the flows that hold stock pass, including:
- `stock-hold-write-confirmation`, `stock-reading`, `lock-acknowledgment`, `stock-availability-required` and `stock-expiry-confirmation`;
- `cart-stock`.

tsc and eslint are clean.

## Acessibilidade

- **Criteria checked:** none changes. No page, text or control is touched.
- **Method:** code reading, tests and an independent review. Its findings are fixed:
  - the 2-second ceiling on each count's question to Stripe, and a lock sized to cover all of them;
  - the locks renewed together;
  - a checkout closed at Stripe because its hold could not be written now lets its units go once Stripe confirms;
  - a cart test named for what it checks, and a new one for an unreadable count (it throws, holds nothing, lets every lock go).
  - **Left as is:** the renewal and the provisional write are two Redis steps rather than one script. The gap is one round trip against a lock of at least 25 seconds.
- **Steps and decisions:** none for the buyer or the creator.
- **Not checked:** testing with real people (item 202). This remains a gap.

**Also in this PR (queue only):** a dated study for 515 [PF3]. Stripe's hosted Checkout page cannot change shipping by the address typed (docs.stripe.com/payments/checkout/custom-shipping-options, read on 2 November 2026). Shipping by region therefore needs the country chosen before going to Stripe; the alternative, the embedded form, is left to the owner.

No price, limit, commission, flag or gate changes. The same Redis key families and the same Stripe calls; one more Redis write per limited checkout, for the provisional hold.

body:
313 [CV1] unit 3, plus the first step of unit 5 (Claude 2). **Draft.** Updated with main on 4 Nov 2026. No price, visible limit, commission, gate or flag change.

Files:
- **Cost model and tests:** `tests/traffic-cost.ts`, `tests/traffic.test.ts`, `tests/room.test.ts`, `tests/numbers-three.test.ts`, `tests/plan-cost-registry.ts`, `tests/store-data-registry.ts`.
- **Checks replaced by decision:** `tests/plan-margin.test.ts`, `tests/limits-proposal.test.ts` and `tests/pricing-optimization-table.ts` (C2-63 and C2-68, below), and one line under 465 [MR2] in `docs/codex-queue.md`.
- **Application code:**
  - `lib/traffic-rules.ts`: `ROOM_LIVE_PARTS` comment only; the value stays 260.
  - `lib/help-content.ts`: the room sentence, now derived.
  - `lib/stats-report.ts` and `lib/visit.ts`: the busy-day email.
  - `app/api/store/hit/route.ts`, `lib/visit.ts`, `lib/traffic.ts`, `lib/traffic-rules.ts`: link clicks, affiliate visits and funnel steps take a signal from the store's own signal counter.
  - `lib/page-funnel-store.ts`, the affiliate directory and the funnels screen: a step says whether it added someone; a rate is not shown while signals ran out.
  - `lib/data-families.ts`: `nl:busy:` kept 2 days; `nl:traffic:s:`, `nl:traffic:sc:` and `nl:traffic:sshort:` deleted with the store.
  - `lib/redis-memory.ts`: the test Redis honors `EXPIRE … NX/XX`.
- **Generated documents**, regenerated by their scripts: `docs/margin-alignment-2026-10-18.md`, `docs/limits-proposal-2026-10-18.md`, `docs/pack-cost-decomposition-2026-10-18.md`, `docs/pricing-usage-proposal-2026-10-18.md`, and `docs/pricing-optimization-2026-10-18.md` with its two JSON files. Also the test-printed rows of `docs/value-presentation-2026-10-18.md`.

## Unit 3: what a visit costs, as billed
`tests/traffic.test.ts` counts what Upstash bills: each command sent **and each `redis.call` a script runs** (https://upstash.com/docs/redis/overall/billing, read 31 Oct 2026). It fails if a measured path sends a script whose inside is not counted. Each view is held by its total (`firstView <= frontCount + firstOfDay`), not by a difference.

| Billed commands | modeled before | measured | model now |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A store view, returning visitor | 12 | 15; heaviest 21 | `frontCount` 25 |
| The store's first view of the day, somebody new, both records at their most | 12 + 4 | 29 | `frontCount` 25 + `firstOfDay` 4 = 29 |
| The same view when it is the month's hundredth visit (`markMonth`) | said to fit inside `firstOfDay` | 34 | + `monthMark` 5, priced on every visit at 1/50. A month has at most 2 + visits/100 marks; 1/50 covers them from 200 visits, and the smallest plan's month is 3,400 |
| Another page opened | 8 | 10; 11 with the day's record at its most | `laterCount` 11 |
| A page-reading beacon | 1 | 3–4 | `readBeacon` 4 |

**Bytes read and sent through the database**, at Upstash's transfer price (`UPSTASH_MICRO_USD_PER_GB_TRANSFER`, imported from `lib/spend-cost-table.ts`; no new figure typed):
- **The store's record.** A visit reads the whole record 6 times: once per page drawn and once per count signal (`storeForPage`/`storeForHandle`). Each read is priced at `MAX_STORE_BYTES` (1,000,000), as `STORE_RECORD_BYTES` already is for the assistant. The reads are counted in the test's pipeline hook (`STORE_READS`: page 1, count 1, reading 0) and added to `visitCost`, `laterPageCost` and the room's leave. Before the independent review of b6dee28d, no visit paid for them.
- **The count script.** `CAPPED_COUNT` (1,921 bytes) is sent whole with every EVAL. The test measured 1 EVAL per view, 1 per later page and 1 per reading. The live room sends no EVAL.

`visitCost()` at the most: **$0.000264 (main) → $0.000484**. The billed commands make it $0.000304; the six reads of the store's record add $0.00018.

## Signals that are not a page
A click on a store's link, a visit through an affiliate's link and a funnel's step (`app/api/store/hit`, k `l`/`a`/`f`) used to run their counts bounded only by the address's allowance.

Each now takes one signal from the store's own counter (`takeSignal`, key `nl:traffic:s:`), never one of the public requests its pages use. An earlier version of this PR took a page's request for each signal, so a store with a 3-page funnel would have rested at about half its printed visits. That was a practical cut of a visible limit, and the second independent review caught it.

- **The counter's room:** `SIGNALS_PER_VISIT` = 6 per printed visit of the plan (`signalLimitFor`, `lib/traffic-rules.ts`). That is a 3-page funnel (3), an affiliate arrival (1) and 2 link-in-bio clicks. It counts the trial's admitted traffic and the funded window, like the requests.
- **Once the room is spent:** the signal is not counted and the reply is still a silent 204. No page rests because of signals.
- **When a signal is spent:** only when something is really written. `takeSignal(store, write)` takes a place, runs the write and gives the place back when nothing was written:
  - **affiliate visit:** `recordClick` runs inside the signal, so a made-up code, a click already counted that day and one over `CLICK_IP_LIMIT` spend nothing;
  - **funnel step:** spends only when the step's PFADD added someone;
  - **link click:** spends only after the link is found and the visitor is not a bot;
  - **owner, team and bots:** never spend one.
- **One connection cannot spend them all:** each connection may spend at most `clientDayShare` of the store's signals a day (408 on Store), key `nl:traffic:sc:`.
- **When the signals run out:** the store gets the mark `nl:traffic:sshort:`. While it holds, the affiliate directory no longer shows the share of clicks that became a sale or what 100 clicks earned. It says "Not complete this month: more clicks came than the plan counts." (or, for an earlier month, that some were not counted). The funnel screen says the same in place of its ratio. A rate is never shown from a count that stopped.
- **Before the store record is read:** `withinLimit` per address and handle, and a per-store lock (`HIT_STORE_LIMIT` = 3,000 per 10 minutes), both run before `storeForHandle`, so a refused POST never reads the store record.
- **Its own cost line:** `signals` in `tests/plan-cost-registry.ts`, at the dearest path measured on the real route.

| Signal path | Commands (measured) |
| --- | --- |
| Link click (first of the day, day record under its cap) | 17 |
| Affiliate visit | 16 |
| Affiliate from a paid ad, with another affiliate's session cookie | 19 |
| Funnel step | 13 |
| Free-trial store (after its first signal) | 16 (+1 pool read in `nonPayingWorst`) |

`COMMANDS.signal` = 19. The bytes read (at most 893) are priced at 8,000. `countRequest` and `takeSignal` write the counter and its `EXPIRE … NX` in one pipeline (`REQUEST_COMMANDS` 1 → 2).

**Help:** the visits and affiliates answers say, from `SIGNALS_PER_VISIT`, how many clicks, arrivals and steps a month the plan counts: 20,400 on Store, 60,000 on Studio, 240,000 on Scale. The directory answer says why a rate may not be shown. The Terms say nothing about counting clicks, so they are unchanged.

**Not measured yet:** the funded window's path (`reservePaidResourceWindow`). It must be measured before `commercialMarginReady` is switched on, and the code says so.

**Not in this PR, sent to Claude 1 for a decision:** the product records read during a visit outside the store's head. Priced at the most each can weigh, the patch is ready, but it breaks three sanity ceilings and the 60% floor of option A in `pricing-optimization` (MR2). Search, bundle items on the front page and collection pages also read records with no ceiling of their own. They need a byte ceiling in code before they can be priced.

## The busy-day email (`maybeBusyAlert`)
Before this change, every power of two from 64 read the creator's choice and 14 days of views before the day's SET NX, even when no email went out. Now:
- **The claim.** The first power of two of the day claims the day (`SET NX`) **before any read**, with a **60-second expiry** (`BUSY_CLAIM_SECONDS`). It keeps the 14 days it read for 2 days, written with `SET XX` (`nl:busy:{day}:{handle}:before`, in the existing `nl:busy:` family, now `Cr(2)`).
- **A failed read.** The claim is deleted at once, best effort, so the next power of two retries.
- **A request that dies** (function timeout). The empty claim lapses after a minute. Before C2-67 it was kept 2 days and the day's email was lost.
- **Later powers of two** that day read the days back in one command, and nothing more once the email has gone.
- **The email** is still deduplicated by the existing `nl:busy:{day}:{handle}` claim, and still never goes to a store whose creator stopped the numbers emails.

**Measured in `tests/numbers-three.test.ts`:** 18 commands for the day's first ask, 7 for the one that sends, and 1 for a later one. The fortnight is read once. Two scenarios each fail with the old code (3 checks each):
- A failed read at 64: 128 reads the days and sends, once.
- A dead request's claim: 128 waits; after the claim lapses, 256 sends, once.
